_comment: Physics profile for the bimanual OpenArm v1.0 under Isaac Sim, consumed by run_isaac_sim.py.
The single-arm profile is openarm.json; everything here is that arm twice, in the joint
order the description emits (left first, then right). Joint names, home pose and the hand's
command interface must match the IsaacArmSystem / IsaacHandSystem blocks in
_home_comment: Both arms at the same pose. joint4's range is [0, 2.443], so 0.0 would rest it on the lower stop; 0.3 lifts it off. Matches home_position in cho_bringup_openarm/config/isaac/controllers_bimanual.yaml.
_armature_comment: Damiao rotor inertia, same values as openarm.json: j1,j2 DM8009 0.0081  j3,j4 DM4340 0.1600  j5,j6 DM4310 0.0100  j7 DM3507 0.0049. It has to be mirrored in the controller's rotor_inertia parameter or the inertia-weighted law commands the wrong torque - on joint3 the rotor is sixteen times the link inertia.
_position_gain_comment: Isaac position-drive gains, per radian. Sized from the arm's own gravity load, not
copied from another robot: k_i = max|tau_gravity,i| over the whole joint-limit box
(40k Pinocchio samples of the URDF) divided by a 1.89 mrad per-joint sag budget.
That budget is 0.015/sqrt(7)/3 - the action server compares the 7-joint error NORM
against 0.015 rad, so seven joints share it, and 3x is the margin.
Damping is critical for the drive alone, d_i = 2*sqrt(k_i * M_ii,max), with M_ii the
diagonal inertia including the rotor at its worst pose. PhysX and Newton both
integrate these drives implicitly, so high stiffness costs no discrete stability.
The previous values [800,800,500,500,120,120,120] came from this project's MuJoCo
actuator file (xml/openarm_v10/actuators_position.xml), where a position actuator's
kp is a different quantity. They happened to pass at the usual test pose (worst
joint 0.0058 rad) but leave a worst-case norm of 0.0198 rad, i.e. over threshold at
the far end of the workspace; these give 0.0045.
joint1 carries zero gravity torque at every pose (it rotates about the vertical), so
it is sized with joint2 rather than left arbitrarily soft.
_torque_damping_comment: Per-motor joint damping from openarm_mujoco v2. Viscous, so it costs nothing at rest; what it buys is the dissipation the controller's own damping cannot supply until a ROS round trip later. Scaling it down to the Franka profile's 0.172 was measured to make the wrist markedly worse.
_hand_gain_comment: The grippers are position-driven in every control mode, as in MuJoCo. Prismatic (0 - 0.044 m), so N/m and N*s/m.
_friction_comment: PhysX joint friction COEFFICIENT, not a torque. Same 0.01 as the single arm: it is what holds the arms still at rest (0 leaves the home pose drifting), and the standing offset it leaves is what sets the controller bandwidth.
_newton_comment: PhysX-only keys, mostly. Newton ignores every physx* attribute here: it takes the drive
gains from UsdPhysics.DriveAPI (authored before play, exactly as the PhysX path does -
the per-degree scaling is right for both) and everything else from its own defaults.
Those gains do double duty on Newton: its importer reads them to decide whether each DOF
gets a POSITION actuator, a VELOCITY actuator or neither, and no runtime call revises
that. A DOF with both gains zero gets no actuator and silently ignores position and
velocity targets - which is why run_isaac_sim.py selects the 'physics' Physics variant
for Newton rather than the 'mujoco' one Newton's own auto-switch picks: 'mujoco' carries
no DriveAPI at all, so every DOF came out unactuated. Torque was unaffected (effort goes
straight to joint_f and needs no actuator), which is exactly why it went unnoticed.
arm_armature IS still applied at runtime through the tensor API: USD-authored
'newton:armature' is deprecated in this release and physxJoint:armature is ignored.
Two values have no Newton equivalent. joint_friction cannot be set at all - the
articulation view's set_dof_friction_properties is a logged no-op in Isaac Sim 6.0.1 -
so under Newton the joints carry no Coulomb friction. Newton also enforces no effort
limit: it reports 1e6 Nm per DOF, so the controller's own clip_torque against the URDF
limits is the only bound on a torque command.
The missing friction helps rather than hurts: the standing offset it causes under PhysX
is what forced the integral term in cho_bringup_openarm/config/isaac/controllers.yaml,
and Newton holds a pose to 0.0000 rad where PhysX settles around 0.006-0.027.
torque, position and velocity are all verified on both engines, single arm and bimanual.
solver_position_iterations and solver_velocity_iterations are PhysX-only; Newton uses
its own solver defaults.
